g.text: Part 2: Federated Connector 3LO Authentication Flow (Components & Steps 1–11)
How a Custom UI and Backend authenticate a Gemini Enterprise Federated Connector via GE Server, GE FE OAuth Redirect Handler, and Keystore

svg.text: Google Cloud — Gemini Enterprise Managed Services

g.text: After Step 11 (or when Step 2 already finds a valid token in Keystore): Querying :streamAssist
Customer BE calls POST .../assistants/default_assistant:streamAssist with toolsSpec.vertexAiSearchSpec.dataStoreSpecs for each connector.
1. Customer UI loads connector UI elements from Customer BE.
2. Customer BE calls GE Server (GET widgetConfigs +
POST dataConnector:acquireAccessToken) with the user's token.
3. GE Server returns the connector list and authUri for any
connector the user has not yet authorized in Keystore.
4. Customer BE returns the connectors & authUri to Customer UI,
which displays an Authorize button if authUri is present.
5. User clicks Authorize. Customer UI opens a popup window to
start the 3LO flow at the 3P Auth Server.
6. After login & consent at the 3P Auth Server, the popup is
7. GE FE Server (/oauth-redirect) posts the code and state
(fullRedirectUri) back to the parent Customer UI window.
Phase 3: Store Token in Keystore & Confirm (Steps 8–11)
8. Customer UI (parent window) sends the callback code & state
(fullRedirectUri) to Customer BE to complete authorization.
GE Server exchanges code at the 3P token API and stores the
user's refresh_token and access_token in Keystore.
10. GE Server returns "connector authorized" status to Customer BE.
11. Customer BE returns "connector authorized" status to Customer UI.
exchanges 3P auth codes for tokens, and manages Keystore storage.
Google-hosted redirect handler that receives the 3P callback and
posts code & state back to the parent Customer UI window.
